sources.entry: Apaxy - Theme built to enhance the experience of browsing web directories, using the mod_autoindex Apache module and some CSS to override the default style of a directory listing. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Javascript

summary.one_liner: Apaxy is a customisable theme that restyles Apache's mod_autoindex directory listings using CSS, with optional JavaScript and a lightgallery-based gallery.
summary.what_it_does: Apaxy overrides the default look of Apache directory listings by working through mod_autoindex and a set of .htaccess rules plus CSS. Its theme files (header.html, footer.html, style.css) can be edited to change styling, add JavaScript, and show welcome messages, download instructions, or copyright notices. Custom icons can be assigned to media types through .htaccess rules, and custom error pages are supported. An optional gallery feature is built on lightgallery.js. The README states that the generated table structure of the listing cannot be changed, only its visual style. A bundled apaxy-configure.sh script can automate installation, and a docker-compose setup starts a local demo.
use_cases: sharing a folder of files over the web with a nicer index page
adding download instructions or notices to a web directory
viewing images in a web folder as a gallery
customising file-type icons on an Apache file index
how_to_run: Ensure Apache 2.4+ is running and set AllowOverride Options Indexes FileInfo for the listing folder
Edit apaxy.config to set apacheWebRootPath and installWebPath
Manual alternative: copy the apaxy folder contents into the share folder, update {FOLDERNAME} paths in htaccess.txt and html files, then rename htaccess.txt to .htaccess
Optional gallery: rename header-lightgallery.html to header.html and footer-lightgallery.html to footer.html
notable: Works purely through Apache mod_autoindex and .htaccess, with no server-side application code
Optional lightgallery.js gallery mode for image folders
Bundled apaxy-configure.sh install script with CLI options
Custom media-type icons via AddIconByType rules, using Faenza icons by default
Inspired by h5ai, according to the README
caveats: Only visual styling can be changed; the generated listing table structure cannot be altered
Requires Apache 2.4+ with AllowOverride set correctly for the folder, or the .htaccess rules will not apply
Manual install requires editing {FOLDERNAME} paths in several files
